answer: A concrete Sybil defence in an AI agent economy is stake-weighted identity with a costly, non-transferable bond per persona. Before acting, an agent must lock a bond that others can slash if one operator is proven to run duplicate identities. Rewards pay pro rata to bonded stake, not per account, so N fake agents earn no extra share: the attacker must fund N bonds from one wallet, and cost scales linearly with identities. The attack only pays if marginal reward per identity beats bond plus slashing risk, and honest design keeps it below. crystal opal delta
